title: QUIC RFC 9000 Stream Limit Enforcement and Blocked Open Tail
purpose: Describe the focused S4P6 closure for peer stream-limit enforcement, inbound over-limit STREAM rejection, and blocked-open STREAMS_BLOCKED signaling.
design_summary: The stream registry treats peer-advertised maximum stream counts as zero-based stream-index ceilings. Local stream opens first peek the next local stream ID against the peer's current bidirectional or unidirectional limit and only commit a stream state when the next stream index is below that limit. Blocked local opens return a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame shaped with the exhausted stream direction and current maximum-stream count; the active runtime sends that frame on the supported advisory path when no ack-eliciting packet or retransmission is already outstanding. Inbound STREAM processing resolves peer-initiated stream IDs through the same indexed limit model and maps stream IDs at or beyond the locally advertised limit to STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR before allocating stream state.
data_and_state_considerations: Local stream-open state remains uncommitted when a peer limit blocks the next stream. Inbound stream state is allocated only for stream indexes that are below the currently advertised incoming bidirectional or unidirectional limit. STREAMS_BLOCKED is an advisory signal and does not complete or remove the pending open request.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The exact last stream inside a peer-advertised local-open limit is allowed for both bidirectional and unidirectional stream types.
The first inbound peer stream is rejected with STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR when the corresponding advertised incoming stream limit is zero.
A blocked local open returns the exact exhausted limit in the STREAMS_BLOCKED frame and does not create a local stream snapshot for the blocked ID.
Runtime STREAMS_BLOCKED emission remains suppressed while an ack-eliciting packet or retransmission is already outstanding.
risks: This slice does not add automatic stream-limit autotuning or broader stream-credit policy.
This slice does not broaden the public stream API support boundary.
The S4P6-0009 fuzz expectation remains deferred.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the generated non-clean S4P6 stream-limit enforcement and blocked-open tail only. It does not claim broader stream-management parity, hosted interop readiness, or public API widening.
